  "overall_assessment": "No concrete severe server/runtime performance blocker is established by the bounded package. One remaining consumer projection issue is reported as nonblocking for this performance dispatch. This assessment uses only the embedded source and evidence; no tools, tests or independent hash verification were performed.\n\nPerformance: the changed saved-observation projector resolves the current same-account association and performs at most two exact observation lookups. It projects only the selected operation, without provider calls, writes or per-history hydration. The unchanged list query materializes the parent page before child hydration; current PostgreSQL plans retain 20/50 operation probes for returned pages and zero probes beyond the last page. Detail hydration remains bounded to 11 operations and 10 receipts each, and catalogue hydration uses one SQL statement with at most 50 indexed probes. Deep OFFSET, exact counts and bounded per-item catalogue writes retain their disclosed costs; the package supplies no fresh severe regression warranting reopening those decisions.\n\nThe UI completion authority uses constant-size metadata, and catalogue flight coalescing reduces duplicate requests. The current browser evidence separately establishes 100 actual BFF requests with 99 blocked 202 responses and one completed provider leader, then 100 UI attempts coalesced into one BFF request with PAUSED/ineligible editor and catalogue outcomes. The 100 independent account intents demonstrate concurrency across distinct resources. The five-tenant RLS stage establishes bounded functional outcomes rather than capacity, latency or saturation. Pending pcv-1 rows still require formal disposition; these markers alone do not close them.\n\nAdherence and structure: the supplied corrections address the prior stale editor hydration, blocked-202 authority, same-account reload and observation-time findings. Context/editor checks precede recovery hydration; derived reads inherit their originating intent; passive reads do not promote completion authority. Later sequential draft reads now supply current operation metadata and matching receipts. Current-context priority precedes context-relative fence comparison, and positive draft proof requires matching non-null semantic fingerprints. Seller submission, immutable operation/ACK associations, separate management credentials, observational GETs, explicit recovery and the narrow Channel boundary remain preserved. The finding concerns how a draft projection's eligibility is merged into the common catalogue, without challenging the accepted ACK design.\n\nElegance: the shared authority and selector are proportionate to the approved race semantics. They avoid additional HTTP reads, caches, endpoints or a generic state framework. Structural soundness and operational fit are mixed because draft-specific and common eligibility still overlap in the shared eligible field at equal fences.\n\nEvidence calibration: the supplied r30 receipt reports 789 passing tests, including 398 PostgreSQL cases and 69 browser cases plus one pure consumer case, with current source/served attribution and all five template markers. Earlier RED limits remain accurately bounded: the r21 derived case did not reach its oracle, r27 lacks its setup-log prefix, r28 did not inspect the final catalogue response, and r29 failed on its first merge order. Original test-after/unknown debt remains closed as recorded process debt. Empty-200 browser coverage remains an explicit uncertainty rather than an established failure.\n\nSEC-R6-04 remains deferred through foundation_documentation/backlog/README.md#BLG-leadshug-template-recovery-read-budget for the private local cohort only; this delta does not invalidate that restriction. Operator-confirmed credential revocation/disablement establishes reported containment with the recorded historical limits. Preserved TEST migration, source-bound activation, actual Meta submission/status and fresh final review remain pending. The activation plan retains bounded metadata preflight, migration timeouts and fail-closed handling. This review grants no delivery or runtime approval.",
  "recommended_path": "Accept the performance corrections at candidate scope without another performance-driven redesign. Route OPS-R3-01 to the observation/adherence owner for narrow correction or explicit disposition. Preserve the private-cohort recovery-budget restriction and complete the remaining independent assurance, formal PCV, preserved TEST preflight, activation, actual provider proof and final review gates.",

      "finding_id": "OPS-R3-01",

      "title": "Equal-fence merging can apply draft-specific ineligibility to the common catalogue",
      "rationale": "Nonblocking under this dispatch's severe-runtime threshold. In web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:123, the equal-fence branch combines eligible with current.eligible && candidate.eligible. TemplateObservationService.projectSavedObservation explicitly sets eligible=false when the saved draft definition differs or its ACK conflicts with the associated resource, while getCatalog/projectRow can correctly return eligible=true for the same current APPROVED, supported observation. Both projections carry the same remote ID and observation fence. Merging that draft observation into the common page therefore makes the catalogue ineligible even with draftScoped=false. The recent eligibility correction removes the eligibleForUse veto, but the contaminated eligible field still vetoes the common result. Consequently, opening a restricted draft can change an otherwise eligible account asset's catalogue presentation. This contradicts the package's explicit distinction between draft association restrictions and common catalogue eligibility. It is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed reproduction, and does not reopen durable ACK association semantics.",
      "suggested_action": "A (recommended): preserve common-producer eligibility for catalogue presentation while retaining definition/ACK restrictions in the draft-scoped proof; keep genuinely unavailable or ineligible common observations restrictive. Resolve this within the existing owner without additional requests or frontend recomputation of backend eligibility. B: distinguish common observation eligibility and draft association eligibility explicitly in internal projection types, with contract review if public fields change. C: record the conservative catalogue false-negative as bounded nonblocking debt with an owner and follow-up. Verify equal-fence common APPROVED/eligible=true plus an actual draft projection restricted by definition mismatch or ACK conflict, in both merge orders: catalogue remains eligible, editor remains restricted, and common available=false or eligible=false still blocks both.",
      "affected_paths": [
        "web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:123",
        "web-app/src/telas/Modelos.spec.ts",
        "api-app/src/domain/message-templates/template-observation.service.ts"
      ]
    }
  ]
